cover_lines: Q3 sales climb as unsold stock builds
Blue Line, Pink Line and suburban rail
cover.headline: Bengaluru Builds Out: Rail, Roads and Townships
cover.subhead: Sales are recovering, launches are heavy and infrastructure timelines keep shifting. What it means for buyers across the city and its fast-growing edges.

editor_note.text: The latest quarter brought a firmer market. According to ANAROCK, Bengaluru housing sales rose 12% YoY to 16,670 units in Q3 2026. The agency also says MMR and Bengaluru together accounted for 48% of total sales across the seven cities it tracks, a reminder of how much national demand now rests on these two markets.

Jobs continue to underpin that demand. Colliers says Bengaluru led Jan-Sep 2026 office leasing at 15.7 million sq ft, driven partly by GCCs and flex operators. ANAROCK adds that GCCs made up 70% of the roughly 10.8 million sq ft of office absorption in H1 2026. Where offices cluster, housing follows.

Infrastructure is the other half of the story, and timelines deserve a careful read. BMRCL's Blue Line has reached 72% overall construction progress, per Business Today, yet Construction World reports the full opening has slipped to March 2028. K-RIDE says it is committed to starting suburban rail operations by December 2028. Buy for today's connectivity, not tomorrow's.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Blue Line (Phase 2A) KR Puram-Central Silk Board
insights.title: Construction World reported on 28 October 2026 that trial runs on Namma Metro's 19.75-km KR Puram-Central Silk Board (Blue Line) stretch are expected to begin by end-October, with overall construction 87 per cent complete.

insights.subject: Hebbal metro land acquisition deposit
insights.title: Asianet Newsable reported on 27 October 2026 that the Supreme Court allowed BMRCL to proceed with construction at Hebbal and that over ₹20.31 crore has been deposited with KIADB toward land-acquisition compensation.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Pink Line elevated section (Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere)
insights.title: Karnataka minister Krishna Byre Gowda said on 28 October that the 7.5-km elevated Pink Line (Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere) has received CMRS safety clearance; the report says the inauguration is planned around PM Modi's proposed 15 November Bengaluru visit, with passenger service dependent on separate authorisation and no start date confirmed.

insights.subject: Bengaluru PG accommodations – Karnataka HC and GBA enforcement
insights.title: On 27 October the Karnataka High Court (Justice Suraj Govindaraj) allowed the GBA to seal illegally operating PGs after repeated non-compliance; a GBA audit of 5,480 PGs found 3,597 operating without licences.

insights.subject: GBA 'Ward One' civic campaign
insights.title: The Bengaluru Live reported on 28 October that the Ward One drive will jointly tackle potholes, broken footpaths, faulty streetlights and leaking water lines; the wards have not been named.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Pink Line elevated corridor (Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere)
insights.title: The Hindu reported on 28 October that Chief Minister said the elevated Pink Line corridor of Namma Metro is likely to be inaugurated on November 15.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Pink Line elevated section
insights.title: Deccan Herald reported on 29 October that Prime Minister Modi is likely to inaugurate the elevated Pink Line next month. Search summary of the article attributes the Nov 15 visit to CM D K Shivakumar; the article itself could not be opened.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Pink Line elevated section
insights.title: Deccan Herald reported that the elevated Pink Line has received a safety nod and may open on November 3 or 15, dates tied to possible Prime Minister visits. Publication date not visible; it appears to be within the window.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Pink Line 7.5 km elevated stretch
insights.title: The Times of India reported on 28 October that the 7.5km Pink Line will take Bengaluru's Metro network beyond 100km. Only the headline was seen.
